Search works now. Let me fetch the core sources.I couldn't write these notes. My research tools stopped working before I could read any of the commentary pages, and I won't fill the gaps from memory because your rules say to report only what the pages actually say.

**What happened:**
- My first attempt to fetch the pages was refused because I'd hit the tool-call limit for that turn. The next two calls timed out.
- One search did work. It found the Enduring Word page for this chapter (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/leviticus-19/), titled "Leviticus 19 Commentary: Many Various Laws". The search only returned a short snippet about treating workers fairly and doing business honestly, which isn't enough to support any verse notes.
- After that, every further call was refused because the tool-use limit had been exceeded. That included the pages from Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, and the commentary on preceptaustin.org.

**What I didn't get to:**
- **Traditional readings:** none of the verse-by-verse commentaries (Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Precept Austin, StudyLight).
- **Protestant differences:** Reformed, Baptist, Methodist, Pentecostal and Lutheran pages. Likely topics would be the Sabbath (v. 3, 30), mixed kinds (v. 19), tattoos (v. 28) and how the law applies to Christians today.
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes, Bible Odyssey, and Catholic and Orthodox sources such as the Catholic Encyclopedia on newadvent.org and catholic.com. Likely topics would be "love your neighbor" (v. 18), the slave girl (v. 20–22) and mediums (v. 31).

When the tools are available again, ask me to run this again. I'll read each page directly and give you notes for v. 1–37 with a URL on every point.
